gaps.sentence: They can't help ___ at his impression of the boss.
gaps.explanation: can't help + -ing = can't stop yourself: can't help laughing.

gaps.sentence: She's considering ___ the flat and moving to the coast.
There's no point ___ about it now.
gaps.explanation: there's no point + -ing: no point worrying.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford ___ another month abroad.
We mustn't miss ___ this exhibition — it ends on Sunday.
We stopped at a village ___ some lunch.
gaps.explanation: stop to do = pause in order to do something: stopped to have lunch.

gaps.sentence: On the way to Rome we stopped ___ some photos.
gaps.hint: stop in order to do sth
gaps.explanation: stop to do = pause in order to do; stop doing = finish doing. Here they paused to take photos.
Negative infinitive: promised not to be late — 'not' goes before 'to'.
